title: The Reading of Names
author: Hallkeeper Hakra Grumhalm
pages: On Hall Night the doors are shut at dusk and no one leaves until dawn. The Hallkeeper reads every name in the hall from the oldest to the newest, and the living answer for each: remembered.
If a name is read and no one answers, the Hallkeeper waits the length of a breath, then answers herself. No name in this hall goes unanswered. That is the oath of my office.
For the newly dead: the body is washed, the beard braided and bound with the clan cord, the deeds spoken. They are laid in the niche, and the Graven Priest seals it with the carved stone.
Their name is cut deep, with their deeds and their debts. If a debt is unpaid the kin must balance it, or it is carved on their stones too. We do not bury debts. We inherit them.
Never open a sealed niche. Never, for any reason, call one of the dead back. If you hear a name read in an empty hall, leave by the main gate, and tell the Lawspeaker before you sleep.
